doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Other instruments he has played or bought
summary: Carter has no instrument he wishes he had learned; he bought a violin only to learn about it for writing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: We’ve sort of covered all the instruments that you’ve played and recorded on, and some that you played and didn’t record on. Are there any that you haven’t played that you would have . . .
. . . or some that you have never played that you have a feeling you might like to try out?

No, I can’t think that . . . no, I mean, if I was twenty years old, there would be things I might like to try out. But I don’t know. No, I never had that feeling. Huh. No, no. And there are a lot of musicians that play all of those instruments. Not necessarily with the greatest ability, but they play the instruments, you know. So I don’t think it’s at all unusual.
I once saw you—I shouldn’t say fiddling around—strumming around with a guitar.

Oh, well, that’s because it happened to be in the house, but if you look in there, you’ll see a violin case, too, and believe me, there’s a violin in it, I think. [laughter] I haven’t opened it in a long time.
I did buy it, but I never played it.
Well, did you buy it with the intention of perhaps playing it?
I bought it with the intention of learning more about the instrument, for the writing.
Yeah, but never intending to really play.
